questions.q: What does a report type decide?
options: Which objects and fields a report can use
Whether the results are shown as a chart or a table
Who is allowed to schedule the report
How many rows the report can be exported with
questions.explain: The report type defines the primary object, its related objects, and the fields available. Layout is a separate choice called the report format.

questions.q: Which of these is a report format rather than a report type?
options: Opportunities with Products
Accounts with Contacts
Matrix
Cases
questions.explain: Tabular, Summary, Matrix, and Joined are formats. The others name objects or object relationships, so they are report types.

questions.q: Which T-SQL idea is closest to choosing a report type?
options: Choosing an ORDER BY column
Deciding which tables to join before writing the query
Adding a HAVING clause
Creating an index
questions.explain: A report type is effectively a pre-built join. It decides which objects and relationships are available before you choose any columns.

questions.q: In a custom report type, what does "A with or without B" behave like?
options: An inner join, keeping only records that have a related B
A left join, keeping records of A even when no B exists
A UNION of A and B
A cross join of every A with every B
questions.explain: "A with B" acts like an inner join. "A with or without B" keeps A records that have no related B, like a left join.

questions.q: While building a report, the Report Builder preview shows only a limited number of records. What should you do to see the full result?
options: Nothing; the preview always shows every record
Delete the filters
Run the report (for example Run or Save & Run)
Change the report format to Joined
questions.explain: The preview is intentionally limited so the builder stays responsive. Running the report shows the complete results.
